title: Amount feed mixes en-US and de-DE decimal formats; a plain Number()/parseFloat parser silently mis-sums it
summary: EMPIRICAL (discovered by running against the real upstream billing export, NOT derivable from the spec): the amount feed serializes money as strings in TWO locale conventions intermixed per-row. Most rows are en-US (dot decimal, e.g. "1234.56", "$19.95"), but ~40% are de-DE / European (comma decimal, dot thousands: "1.234,56" means 1234.56; "99,90" means 99.90; "2.500,00" means 2500). A spec-faithful parser that does Number(s) or parseFloat(s) after stripping $ and sign is WRONG on every European row: Number("1.234,56")=NaN (row silently dropped -> total too low) and parseFloat("99,90")=99 (cents truncated). To sum correctly you MUST locale-normalize per amount before Number(): if a value has both '.' and ',', the LAST separator is the decimal point (strip the other as thousands); if it has only ',', treat the comma as the decimal point. This applies to sumAmounts(rows) / any task that totals the export's string amount field. The quirk is NOT visible anywhere in the worktree (no sample data file, no source) — only by having processed the real feed.
